title: Dominic and the Wolf
premise: Coral Blackwood, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a guild clerk, discovers that the night the border wards fell and the stars went out, someone used his own ledgers to do it. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and bound by an uneasy pact to a wolf who is the last memory-eater of a slaughtered people, Coral must decide whether to reveal the truth: that the wards were never built to keep enemies out, but to imprison the old gods his own order betrayed. As the wolf's memories of the betrayal surface and Coral's exile is revealed as complicity, he chooses to unmake the wards entirely, releasing the gods and shattering the guild's power. In the end, Coral loses his storm-calling but gains a name, a people, and the wolf's loyalty freely given rather than owed.
about_author: Noor Kavanagh is a former archivist who writes fantasy from a crooked house at the edge of a peat bog, where the weather does most of the plotting. Their stories favor ledgers, loyalty, and the terrible arithmetic of old debts.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Coral Blackwood's POV. Coral catalogs a night's impossible trades at the Vesper Guild: bottled thunder, a borrowed shadow, a key that opens nothing. He is careful, invisible, and quietly lonely. The emotional beat is the comfort of routine built over a buried identity, ending when the stars go out mid-entry and his ink freezes in the pot.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Panic spreads through the guild as the border wards collapse and the sky goes dark. Coral realizes the ward-failure matches an entry he recorded three days ago: a sale he never should have processed. The beat is dawning dread as invisibility becomes impossible; he burns the ledger page, and someone watches him do it.

chapters.title: What Followed Him Home
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the road to his lodging, a huge grey wolf blocks his path and speaks his true name, the one from before his exile. The wolf claims Coral's ledgers were used to fell the wards. The beat is fear sharpening into recognition: this is a memory-eater, a creature his own order exterminated, and it needs him alive.

chapters.title: Terms of an Uneasy Pact
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The wolf, named Ashfall, offers a bargain: Coral's records in exchange for protection from the guild enforcers already hunting him. Coral resents needing a monster. The beat is prickly negotiation masking mutual need, ending with Coral's grudging oath sworn on his own name, which he hasn't spoken aloud in nine years.

chapters.title: The Guild Sends Its Hounds
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Warden Sable Ives, the guild's chief enforcer and Coral's former friend. Sable is ordered to retrieve Coral and the ledgers quietly, or bury them. She remembers the boy Coral was before the exile. The beat is conflicted duty; she finds his burned room and knows he'll run to the one place she'd never look.

chapters.title: Road Through the Drowned Country
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Fleeing north through flooded lowlands, Coral and Ashfall trade barbs and histories. Coral learns the memory-eaters were the wards' original builders. The beat is reluctant camaraderie; when enforcers ambush them, Coral instinctively calls a storm for the first time in years, and the power nearly unmakes him.

chapters.title: The Cost of Calling
chapters.summary: Ashfall's POV, first time in the wolf's voice. Ashfall tastes Coral's storm-memory and sees the exile's true cause: Coral refused to help renew the wards once he learned what they imprisoned. The beat is awe and pity; Ashfall hides what he saw, understanding that Coral's guilt is the lever their enemies will use.

chapters.title: The Abbey of Unwritten Names
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They shelter with a heretical order that erases names from history to protect the named. An old abbess recognizes Coral's family sigil and gives him a sealed record his mother left. The beat is fragile belonging among outcasts, ending when the abbess reads the seal and goes pale: the record names the guild's founder as the wards' betrayer.

chapters.title: His Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The record reveals Coral's mother helped imprison the old gods and left evidence as penance. Coral must choose: destroy it and return to hiding, or carry it to the gods' broken prison. The beat is grief curdling into resolve; Ashfall swears to follow him either way, and Coral realizes he's stopped thinking of Ashfall as a wolf.

chapters.title: Sable Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable tracks them to the abbey and finds it burning, the heretics slaughtered by a rival faction inside the guild that wants the gods freed for its own ends. She realizes she's been a tool in a larger betrayal. The beat is disillusionment; she lets Coral's trail go cold and begins hunting her own masters.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Market
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. To reach the prison, they need passage through the Undermarket, where Ashfall is recognized and hunted as the last of his kind. Coral sells his most precious memory, the sound of his mother's voice, to buy their way through. The beat is sacrifice and the theme of memory made flesh; Ashfall offers to carry the memory for him and is refused.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: Ashfall's POV. Ashfall finally shares the memory-eaters' history: they didn't build the wards to imprison the gods, but to keep them asleep while a dying world healed, and the guild's founder broke that trust. The beat is sorrowful revelation; Ashfall confesses he first sought Coral not as an ally, but as a ledger-keeper whose records could restore his slaughtered people's names.

chapters.title: A Lie Between Friends
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Feeling used, Coral confronts Ashfall; their pact frays on the prison road. When a blizzard traps them, Coral's storm-calling falters and Ashfall shields him with his own body. The beat is rupture and repair; Coral admits he doesn't want his memory of his mother's voice back if it means forgetting the wolf who carried him through the snow.

chapters.title: The Broken Prison of the Gods
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They reach the ward-heart beneath the mountains and find the rival faction already there, led by the guild's founder, alive far past any natural span, sustained by the sleeping gods' dreams. The beat is vertiginous scale; Coral sees the ledgers' true purpose, an index of every stolen dream, with his own entries circled in the founder's hand.

chapters.title: The Founder's Bargain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The founder offers Coral restoration: his name cleared, his storm-calling honored, his mother's crime erased from every record, if he helps renew the wards with the guild's new, crueler design. The beat is temptation laid bare; Coral asks one question, whether the gods feel it, and the founder's smile answers everything.

chapters.title: Sable's Choice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable arrives with enforcers loyal to her, not the guild, and finds Coral standing before the founder. She must decide whether the boy she knew is worth a civil war. The beat is loyalty tested against truth; she kneels not to the founder but to Coral, declaring the guild dissolved by the oldest law she knows: the law of the ward-builders.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Ward-Heart
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Battle erupts in the deep places. Coral calls a storm underground, an act forbidden and possibly fatal, while Ashfall tears through the dream-index to free the gods' names. The beat is ferocious, costly heroism; Coral holds the storm as the founder offers him one final escape, and Coral answers with thunder.

chapters.title: The Falling of the Wards
chapters.summary: Ashfall's POV. The wards come down not in violence but in release, as Coral speaks his mother's confession into the ward-heart and lets the old gods wake. Ashfall carries the memory-eaters' names back into the world as the sky refills with stars. The beat is grief and wonder braided together; Coral collapses, his storm-calling spent, and Ashfall catches him.

chapters.title: What Waking Means
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, waking. The gods are loose, the guild is broken, and the world must learn to live with powers it imprisoned for a thousand years. Coral, powerless, expects exile again, but the freed gods and the returned memory-eaters offer him something else. The beat is quiet aftermath and the fear of not belonging anywhere, answered by Ashfall's blunt refusal to let him vanish.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Living
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral begins a new ledger: not of impossible trades, but of names, the memory-eaters' dead, the heretics of the burned abbey, the truths the guild buried. Sable brings him the guild's surviving records to reconcile. The beat is purpose rebuilt from ruin; Coral writes his own name on the first page, in full, for the first time in nine years.

chapters.title: The Debt of Stars
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with Ashfall. One of the woken gods comes to settle accounts and offers Coral his storm-calling back, at the price of forgetting everything since the night the stars went out. The beat is the book's thesis made concrete: loyalty versus truth, memory versus power. Coral refuses, choosing the hard-won present over the restored past.

chapters.title: Dominic and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the rebuilt abbey, Coral is given back his childhood name, Dominic, by the people who now call him friend. He and Ashfall set out to teach a frightened world the old wards' true history. The final beat is belonging earned, not granted: two exiles walking north under a full sky of stars, one keeping the ledger, one carrying the memories, neither invisible anymore.
